name: What if my Los Angeles home has old plumbing or electrical that needs upgrading?

mainEntity.name: What if my Los Angeles home has old plumbing or electrical that needs upgrading?
mainEntity.text: What if my Los Angeles home has old plumbing or electrical that needs upgrading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes in Los Angeles often reveal plumbing and electrical issues once kitchen demolition begins. If the home still has outdated wiring, undersized circuits, old galvanized pipes, or previous unpermitted modifications, the project may require upgrades before the new kitchen can be installed safely. This affects both the design and the budget, because new appliances, lighting, and ventilation often need more capacity than the original systems provide. The smart move is to inspect those systems before finalizing the kitchen plan, especially if the home is in an older neighborhood with many mid-century or pre-war properties. A well-planned custom kitchen should include enough electrical capacity for modern appliances, task lighting, and code-compliant outlet placement. Plumbing may also need rerouting if the sink, dishwasher, or refrigerator location changes. Homeowners should expect some contingency money in the budget for this reason, because hidden infrastructure work is common in full remodels.
acceptedAnswer.description: Old plumbing or electrical systems can increase cost and extend the timeline of a custom kitchen remodel. These upgrades are common in older Los Angeles homes and should be evaluated early so the design, permit plan, and budget account for them.
